llm.summary: The skill claims to include a self-contained Linux binary but that binary is not in the package; it also points to external downloads and optional report uploads — coherent purpose but several packaging and data-exfiltration risks that need clarification before use.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and INSTALL.md claim a built-in binary at assets/bin/skillscan (with a SHA-256) and describe CLI usage; however the package manifest does not include the binary file itself (only SKILL.md, INSTALL.md, agents/openai.yaml, and assets/build/build-info.json). This mismatch (claimed capability vs actual contents) is incoherent and could be either a packaging mistake or an attempt to get users to fetch a binary from an external URL.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions are narrowly scoped to scanning skill packages (expected). However they also document enterprise integration that uploads full review payloads to an arbitrary upload-url (example: https://scanner.example.com/api/report). Uploading full scan results (which the docs say include 'embedded review details for each skill') is a potential exfiltration vector and should be considered high-sensitivity data. The external-engine option and download instructions increase scope because they cause the agent/user to obtain and run code from outside this package.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec (instruction-only), which is low risk normally — but SKILL.md advertises a built-in binary that is not present, and provides an external download URL (https://clawhub.ai/cyzlmh/cmic-skill-scanner). That external host is not a well-known official release source; instructing users to download/extract/run a binary from an unfamiliar URL raises risk. The package also includes a checksum in build-info.json, but without the binary present the checksum cannot be verified locally.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, credentials, or config paths (appropriate for a scanner). However the documented enterprise upload and external-engine bridge imply network endpoints and possibly credentials (not declared). If used, those options could require tokens or allow data transmission to third parties; those must be explicitly disclosed and justified.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Flags are default: always=false and user-invocable=true; model invocation is allowed (normal). The skill does not request permanent presence or system-level configuration changes in the package contents provided.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is suspicious mainly because it claims to include a Linux binary that is missing from the files you were given and points to an external download and optional upload endpoint. Before installing or running anything: 1) Ask the publisher why the binary is absent and request an official release URL (preferably GitHub releases or another trusted host). 2) If you must run the scanner, do so in an isolated environment (VM/container) and verify any downloaded binary's checksum against a trusted source. 3) Do not enable or provide any upload-url or credentials until you confirm the destination and what data will be sent; enterprise upload could leak full scan contents (including skill package data). 4) Prefer packages from a verifiable homepage or source; lack of a homepage and unknown owner ID reduce trust. If the publisher cannot satisfactorily explain the missing binary and the external endpoints, treat the package as untrusted.
